content:
Looking at the cuboid (3×2×2 = 12 cubes), the visible faces show:
- **Light gray:** front-top-left, front-bottom-left, front-bottom-middle, back-top-left (4 cubes — complete)
- **Dark gray:** front-top-middle, front-top-right, front-bottom-right, back-top-right (4 cubes — complete)
- **White:** back-top-middle and back-bottom-right (visible via orange outlines)

The only unseen cubes are the back-bottom-left and back-bottom-middle. Since light gray and dark gray already have 4 cubes each, these two hidden cubes must be white.

So the white block consists of: the entire bottom row of the back layer (3 cubes) plus the cube on top of the middle of that row — a flat T-shape (row of 3 with one cube on top of the center).

This matches option D.

\boxed{D}
